newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re sees '97 profits up over 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sees '97 profits up over 20 pct.

text.p: Swiss Re chief executive Walter Kielholz said that he expected a profit at the firm in 1997 which would be more than 20 percent higher than that seen in 1996.
"Looking ahead, we expect a profit increase (in 1997) of over 20 percent," Kielholz said in a speech to shareholders.
He also said that the company will provide more information in detail about its 1997 performance in September when it will publish an interim report for the first time.

Kielholz also reiterated the company's forecast for a positive profit contribution resulting from the acquisition of Mercantile and General Reinsurance Co Ltd and from the transaction involving SAFR/Partner Re.

Swiss Re said in April it had completed a takeover of a majority stake in France's Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR). As part of the deal, Swiss Re also would increase its stake in Bahamas-based Partner Re. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
